newsitem.title: DUBAI: Saudi begins construction of $1.7 bln power plant.
newsitem.headline: Saudi begins construction of $1.7 bln power plant.

text.p: Saudi Crown Prince Abdullah on Tuesday laid the foundation stone of a 1,286-megawatt power plant in the capital Riyadh, Saudi state-run television said.
"The plant is part of a 25-year electricity development plan," the television said.
The Saudi daily Al-Iqtisadiyah said the power station was a joint venture between the Saudi Bin Laden Group and General Electric Co.

Abdullah bin Abdul-Rahman al-Tassan, chairman of the Saudi Consolidated Electric Power Company (SCECO) for the central province -- which includes Riyadh -- said the plant would cost 6.49 billion riyals ($1.7 billion).
Its capacity would be raised to 1,930 MW in the future, he said, but gave no details.
Al-Tassan said the first stage of the project, with a capacity of 224 MW, would be operational before next summer.
He said the plant was part of an effort to match the growing demand for electricity in the province, which peaked at 5,423 MW in the past summer, up 300 MW from the previous year.

SCECO's Director General Abdelaziz bin Abdullah al-Abdelwahed said the plant would be run by Saudi nationals. "What calls for pride is that this project will be operated by Saudis. A group has been trained and appointed to operate the first phase," he said.
